body:
Hi I want to write a kernel that dynamically selects which descriptor to use inside the kernel.
(I cannot combine them into one large descriptor since base addresses are not contiguous)

I tried to pass multiple host created descriptors and use conditionals to select inside the kernel:

```python
desc1 = TensorDescriptor(base1, ...)
desc2 = TensorDescriptor(base2, ...)
desc3 = TensorDescriptor(base3, ...)

@triton.jit
def kernel(desc1, desc2, desc3):
    desc_idx = ...  # computed at runtime
    desc = tl.where(desc_idx == 0, desc1, tl.where(desc_idx == 1, desc2, desc3))

    ...
```

But `TensorDescriptor` isn't a tensor, so `tl.where` doesn't work on them.
Even if this was supported, I don't want many conditionals inside my kernel.

I want to do this instead:
```python
desc1 = TensorDescriptor(base1, ...)
desc2 = TensorDescriptor(base2, ...)
desc3 = TensorDescriptor(base3, ...)
desc_ptrs = [desc1.data_ptr(), desc2.data_ptr(), desc3.data_ptr()]

@triton.jit
def kernel(desc_ptrs):
    desc_idx = ...
    desc = tl.gather(desc_ptrs, desc_idx, axis=0) 
```

I can do this trick using pointer indexing (by directly passing torch.tensor), but once I wrap with `TensorDescriptor`, I can't call data_ptr since it is not a torch.tensor anymore..

Is there a supported way to dynamically index into descriptors without descriptor creation inside the kernel?
title: Can I dynamically index into an array of TensorDescriptors at runtime?
